notes: `reports/VerificationTasks.pdf` section 10.1, the preamble to Task 1: check that the directed triangle query `Q(x) :- E(x, y), E(y, z), E(z, x)` and its reformulation `Q↑(x) :- V(x, y, z), V(y, z, x)` agree under `V = E ∘ E`. Global schema `{E}` (binary), local schema `{V}` (ternary) with the LAV view `V(a, b, c) ↔ E(a, b) ∧ E(b, c)`.

The source documents the reformulations task document (sha256 `32a3ac6b428d851f0aaa4fb7acdbf2fe4ad5dacca93ee118837888ff91b7a1c6`) and `reports/VerificationTasks.pdf` (sha256 `796ff97c082c6fc70e75a60c0dd40ec0680b738d7184a8b8aefea8c681b3ebff`) carry the same section 10.1 text, so both name this task.

The command is not hand-authored: `Fidelity/Example4001.lean` states the PDF's two Datalog programs, compiles each with `Datalog.WhielCompiler.Naive`, writes the two compiled commands one after the other, renames the generated snapshots `Q_1` and `QUp_1` to the auxiliary input names `Q_aux` and `QUp_aux`, and proves the result equal to `inputCmd` by `decide +kernel`; the same module fixes `inputPre` as the view constraint and `inputPost` as the claim `Q = QUp` and pins the single loop `Hoare.preprocess` computes from the sequence.

Neither program is recursive. Both are compiled by the same naive compiler anyway, so the canonical input carries exactly one WHILE loop, as `Hoare.preprocess` requires; the joint loop converges after a single iteration.
Verdict valid, certified under set semantics: the triangle query is reconstructed by joining two copies of the path view on overlapping variables.
Reference encoding for intent only: the retired corpus case Example4001, an `IndexAlphaName` hand-written input in the earlier single-level framework. Nothing is copied from it.

The the reference encoding's certified invariant into six leveled-framework clauses over the computed prophecy schema, all prophecy-free and therefore at level 0: `(op_zQ ⊆ π[0] (σ[((#1 = #2 ∧ #3 = #4) ∧ #0 = #5)] ((op_zE × (op_zE × op_zE)))))`, `(op_zQUp ⊆ π[0] (σ[((#1 = #3 ∧ #2 = #4) ∧ #0 = #5)] ((op_zV × op_zV))))`, `(op_zV ⊆ π[0,1,3] (σ[#1 = #2] ((op_zE × op_zE))))`, `(π[0,1,3] (σ[#1 = #2] ((op_zE × op_zE))) ⊆ op_zV)`, `(π[0] (σ[((#1 = #2 ∧ #3 = #4) ∧ #0 = #5)] ((op_zE × (op_zE × op_zE)))) ⊆ op_zQ)` and `(π[0] (σ[((#1 = #3 ∧ #2 = #4) ∧ #0 = #5)] ((op_zV × op_zV))) ⊆ op_zQUp)`. These six rows are now frozen in `Core.json`; the certificate additionally carries the emitter's own definitional clause `(op_zV = π[0,1,3] (σ[#1 = #2] ((op_zE × op_zE))))`, restating the two `op_zV` containments above as one equality, for seven candidate clauses in total.

title: Directed triangle query versus its path-view reformulation
explanation: The two Datalog programs compute the directed-triangle query Q(x) :- E(x,y), E(y,z), E(z,x) over an edge relation E, and its reformulation Q↑(x) :- V(x,y,z), V(y,z,x) over a length-two path view V. Under the view constraint that V records exactly the length-two paths of E together with their midpoint (V = E ∘ E), the Hoare triple claims the two queries compute equal results, Q = Q↑; this is an equivalence claim. The claim is certified valid: joining two copies of the view on overlapping variables reconstructs the directed-triangle detection under set semantics.
preInWords: The precondition states that V equals the set of length-two paths through E: V is E composed with E, projected onto the start, midpoint and end columns with the middle columns equated.
postInWords: The postcondition asserts the two queries agree exactly, Q = QUp.
